short.q: P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.3 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.1. Find P(A ∪ B) and show whether A and B are independent. [4]
short.model: P(A ∪ B) = 0.6 + 0.3 − 0.1 = 0.8. P(A) × P(B) = 0.18, which is not equal to 0.1, so A and B are not independent.

short.q: A bag has 4 green and 6 yellow counters. Two are taken without replacement. Find the probability that both are green, and that at least one is yellow. [4]
short.model: P(both green) = 4/10 × 3/9 = 12/90 = 2/15. P(at least one yellow) = 1 − 2/15 = 13/15.

short.q: P(rain) = 0.2. If it rains, P(late) = 0.5. If it does not rain, P(late) = 0.1. Find P(late), and given that he is late, the probability it rained. [4]
40 students: 25 study French, 18 study Spanish and 8 study both. How many study neither? Find P(Spanish | French). [3]
short.model: French only 17, Spanish only 10, both 8, so 35 study at least one and 5 study neither. P(Spanish | French) = 8/25 = 0.32.

short.q: Explain the difference between mutually exclusive and independent events. [2]
short.model: Mutually exclusive: they cannot happen at the same time, P(A ∩ B) = 0. Independent: one happening does not change the probability of the other, P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).
points: independent: one does not affect the other
